clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs replace the single-trailing-slash strip in buildWellKnownPath with a full trailing-slash strip, but #2214 stops there, leaving shouldAttemptFallback's `pathname === '/'` root check stale: once pathname normalization strips a lone '/' down to '', that check can never fire, so root-like paths would still trigger a redundant fallback request. #2215 introduces a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper and updates shouldAttemptFallback's sentinel to '' to match, closing the exact redundant-fallback bug its own title targets, which #2214 leaves open. #2214 is fully subsumed by #2215's change.

clusters.pick_reason: 2692 settles pending requests with a JSON-RPC error (-32000, 'Connection closed'), matching the existing JSON-RPC error convention used elsewhere in this file, whereas 2600 answers with a bare HTTP 404 'Session not found' that mischaracterizes an in-flight close as a missing session. 2692 also explicitly groups outstanding request ids by shared stream to handle batched POSTs (multiple request ids on one stream) and reuses an already-produced real response instead of overwriting it with an error - neither case is mentioned in 2600's description. 2600 bundles in an unrelated fix (clearing _requestToStreamMapping to stop a correlation leak across storeEvent() awaits); that part is out of scope for the hanging-response bug and, if still needed, should be filed as its own PR rather than folded into this one.

members.title: fix(server): retire in-flight request state when the streamable HTTP transport closes
members.author: rxits
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2692: Both fix the same root bug: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() leaves a JSON-response-mode POST's Promise<Response> unsettled, so the HTTP request hangs until the platform's own timeout instead of resolving when the transport closes. Both change close() to settle the pending response for outstanding request ids before/while tearing down stream mappings, so they touch the same close() logic and would conflict if both merged.
